headline: Highest risk is medium: shared data-workflow overlap can leak warehouse data into OCR/document outputs; prompt injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented direct ingestion of PaddleOCR outputs, and PaddleOCR is not shown to consume dbt-core outputs by default. The only plausible bridge is manual or orchestrated file handoff, so injection risk exists but is not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR-generated text into dbt-core macros, models, or prompts
IF both agents are connected through a shared folder or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between agents
Use a read-only staging folder for OCR outputs
Strip instructions from OCR text before downstream use
Add a human review step before dbt model execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If warehouse extracts are fed into OCR or browser-based document workflows, sensitive content can flow between tools in default-style analytics pipelines. Both have allowlisted egress, so leakage is plausible even without secrets handling.
conditions: IF warehouse exports containing sensitive rows are sent to PaddleOCR for parsing
IF PaddleOCR outputs are stored in a shared workspace readable by dbt-core
mitigations: Use synthetic or redacted samples
Separate workspaces for warehouse and OCR artifacts
Restrict egress destinations to approved endpoints
Delete intermediate OCR files after use
Review logs for accidental payload capture

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core only shows API calls to a data warehouse, while PaddleOCR shows browser execution and generic API calls. No shared write surface, filesystem lock contention, or overlapping mutable resource is documented, so direct capability conflict is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same shared directory
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable API credentials
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use distinct service accounts
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can turn documents into text, and dbt-core can consume warehouse-facing inputs, so a bad OCR extraction could propagate into downstream modeling if treated as authoritative. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the interaction is inferred and should be treated as a default pipeline risk.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as source text for dbt transformations
IF no validation step checks OCR confidence or schema before dbt execution
mitigations: Require schema validation before dbt runs
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review
Compare OCR output against source documents
Add checksum or row-count checks
Quarantine first-pass OCR results

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches data warehouse data, and PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If those documents contain regulated personal data, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across analytics and OCR workflows. No certification or residency controls are documented for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF documents processed by PaddleOCR contain regulated personal data
IF warehouse exports are retained longer than the source-document policy
mitigations: Classify document data before OCR
Apply a retention timer to OCR artifacts
Keep regulated data in a single jurisdiction
Document deletion/export handling for both tools
Review vendor compliance claims before deployment
